name: a null property is omitted like an absent optional, but a null inside an array is kept
source: packages/sdk-android/sdk/src/main/kotlin/io/advenue/core/Json.kt writeObject skips null-valued entries and writeValue keeps them inside arrays; packages/sdk-swift/Sources/AdvenueCore/AdvenueValue.swift now does the same. The two SDKs disagreed: Kotlin omitted, Swift emitted, so one call produced different warehouse rows depending on the platform. The server accepts either — properties are z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) — so nothing broke, which is why nothing noticed. Omission wins because {"x":null} and {} say the same thing to any consumer of an event property, and the 8 KB properties cap makes the difference pure cost. Inside an array the null stays: there is no key to omit and dropping it would shift every element after it.
